title: Non-blocking finding from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups' PR review (#404)
description: pr-reviewer's full review of PR #404 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups) accepted it -- make e2e (28/28, plus a mutation test that temporarily broke the History table's date rendering to confirm the assertion is still load-bearing), static analysis, and coverage all passed, and the waitForResponse-vs-click ordering was verified correct (listener registered before the triggering click via Promise.all, not after). One non-blocking test-infrastructure-convention finding surfaced and shouldn't disappear once PR #404 merges.

checklist.step: frontend/tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts now imports directly from `../../src/api/homework` (a type) and `../../src/utils/format` (a value) -- the first e2e spec in frontend/tests/e2e/ to import anything from `src/` at all; every other spec that needs a shared helper (e.g. portfolio.spec.ts's `isoDateWeeksAgo`) imports it from `tests/dateFixtures.ts` instead, a tests-local module, not application source. This import is correct and was the right fix for the specific duplication finding it closed (the task's checklist explicitly called for importing `formatDate` directly), but it's a new precedent: an e2e spec now has a compile-time dependency on an app-source module's exact path/export shape, which couples a black-box browser-level test to an internal refactor in a way the rest of the suite doesn't. Worth an explicit, recorded convention decision for future specs -- e.g. should an e2e spec import src/ helpers directly when there's no real alternative (as here), or should a shared tests/-local re-export/wrapper be preferred to keep that coupling at one boundary -- rather than leaving it as an ad hoc one-off that future spec authors might copy inconsistently.

decisions.decision: Documented an explicit convention in docs/architecture/Testing.md's "End-to-end (Playwright)" section: an e2e spec may import a *type* or a *pure, side-effect-free utility/formatting function* directly from `src/` (both tsconfigs already cover `src` and `tests` together) when that's needed to assert against the exact value/format the app itself produces -- e.g. daily-homework.spec.ts's `DailyHomeworkOut` type (import type, erased at compile time, zero runtime coupling) and `formatDate` (src/utils/format.ts, a pure function with no React/DOM/app-state dependency). Importing a React component, hook, context, or any module with side effects/DOM/app-runtime dependencies is not allowed, to keep the suite's black-box (real browser, real DOM) boundary intact. A genuinely test-only need shared across specs that isn't a copy/wrapper of app logic (e.g. isoDateWeeksAgo) still belongs in a tests/-local module (tests/dateFixtures.ts), not under src/. Added a short comment to daily-homework.spec.ts itself pointing back to this convention for discoverability. No code change to the spec's imports was needed -- both of its existing src/ imports (a type-only import and a pure utility) already conform to the convention as decided.
decisions.rationale: Rejected two alternatives. (1) Banning all direct src/ imports and requiring every such need to go through a tests/-local re-export/wrapper module: for a type import this adds pure ceremony since a type is erased at compile time and carries zero runtime coupling risk, so wrapping it in a tests/-local re-export doesn't reduce any real coupling, only adds indirection. For a pure value like `formatDate`, a tests/-local wrapper would still have to import it from src/ internally to stay correct -- it relocates where the src/ dependency is declared without removing it, and risks the wrapper itself drifting out of sync with the real helper the way the prior ad hoc inline reimplementation already did (the exact bug frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups fixed by importing the real helper instead of recreating its logic). Importing the real helper directly is what makes the assertion catch genuine app-formatting drift; a wrapper doesn't add that property, it only costs a layer of indirection. (2) Allowing unrestricted src/ imports with no scope limit: rejected because the whole reason this suite exists (per Testing.md's own framing) is to catch disagreement between app code and its own mocked test doubles by driving the real browser/DOM -- a spec that could import and exercise a component or hook directly would let a future spec bypass the browser-level black-box boundary entirely, re-introducing the exact class of gap the mocked unit/component suites and this e2e suite are supposed to catch independently of each other. Scoping the exception to type-only and pure-value imports keeps that boundary intact while still permitting the one case (comparing against the app's actual formatting logic) that genuinely needs it. isoDateWeeksAgo was kept as the precedent for the tests/-local case specifically because it's test-fixture logic that doesn't exist in app source at all (not a copy or wrapper of anything in src/), so there's no inconsistency in treating it differently from formatDate/DailyHomeworkOut.
